title: ACIM-QMM: Efficient Analog Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for QC-MDPC McEliece Cryptosystem
problem: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) implementations like QC-MDPC McEliece suffer from high latency and large hardware overhead in digital computing paradigm.
motivation: Quantum computing threat to current encryption necessitates PQC deployment; QMM requires key generation and encryption operations with high performance demands.
method: ACIM-QMM leverages analog circuits and computing-in-memory to perform matrix operations required for QMM key generation and encryption, breaking the digital computing bottleneck while maintaining low relative error.
key_novelty: First analog CIM accelerator for post-quantum cryptography, using analog computation paradigm to replace digital multiplication-accumulation in PQC algorithms.
contributions: Analog CIM architecture for QC-MDPC McEliece cryptosystem
31.4x to 288.1x speedup compared to SOTA QMM hardware
3.12x area efficiency and 20.32x energy efficiency vs other PQC hardware
Low-error analog computation for cryptographic primitives
primary_theme: analog CIM for post-quantum cryptography acceleration
